paras: The lynching at Winnsborough, Louisiana, was the hanging in late July 1880 of an unnamed seventeen-year-old Black youth, taken from the Franklin Parish jail by "a body of men" and hanged to a tree outside the town. He had been jailed on an accusation of attempting to "outrage" the daughter of a prominent lawyer, and the episode is known only from a short item in an Alexandria weekly quoting a New Orleans dispatch.

According to a dispatch to the New Orleans Times, the youth entered the young woman's room through a window "on Friday two weeks ago" and got into her bed before she discovered him. Her screams woke her father, and the youth jumped from the window and escaped, but he was soon captured by the Sheriff and lodged in jail. The dispatch said he "confessed to the fact" and also admitted that in the past twelve months he had tried to enter almost every house in Winnsborough; it gives no account of how the confession was obtained.

About midnight on the following Saturday, a body of men went to the jail, broke off the lock and took him out. They hanged him to a tree about 100 yards from town, where he was found hanging on Sunday morning. The report names neither the victim nor any of the men and does not state their number.
No report of an inquest, of arrests of the lynchers or of any official response appears in the coverage found.

The Louisiana Democrat of Alexandria carried the story on August 4, 1880, as a brief unheaded item that extracted the New Orleans Times dispatch. The item stated the accusation as fact, calling the youth "a negro boy" who "attempted to outrage a young lady," and recounted the hanging without comment. No other report of the hanging, in either the white or the Black press, was found.

reader.title: Lynching at Winnsborough, Louisiana (1880)
bases: A body of men broke the jail lock, took out a prisoner accused of attempted outrage and hanged him to a tree outside town (A1).

The prisoner was taken from jail by 'a body of men' who broke off the lock and hanged him, with no lawful authority, over an accusation of attempting to outrage a white lawyer's daughter (A1); the number of men is not given, but the collective 'body of men' indicates more than two.
The only report found is a short item in the Louisiana Democrat quoting a dispatch to the New Orleans Times (A1); no local, Black-press or follow-up report was found.

accounts.gist: The youth entered the lawyer's daughter's room, fled when she screamed, was captured by the Sheriff, confessed, and was taken from jail by a body of men about midnight Saturday and hanged near town.
